title: Displacement current & the Ampere paradox
subtitle: Why magnetostatics breaks on a charging capacitor, how Gauss law restores continuity, and the single-surface rule.
takeaway: Evaluate Ic and Id across the SAME spanning surface of loop C; adding both from two surfaces double-counts one current.

cards.title: Why static Ampere law breaks during charging
items: Draw one circular loop C around the wire feeding a charging parallel-plate capacitor. Flat surface S1 cuts the wire (current Ic), whereas bulging surface S2 passes between the plates and cuts zero conduction current.
One closed rim C cannot have two different circulations. Maxwell-Ampere repairs this by adding changing electric flux through whichever single surface spans C.
Never write Ic + Id = 2 Ic on gap surface S2: inside an ideal vacuum gap Ic = 0 and Id = Ic, while on S1 across the wire Id = 0 and Ic = Ic.

cards.title: Charge conservation & the divergence check
items: Because div(curl B) is identically zero for every smooth vector field, the magnetostatic law curl B = mu0 J forces div J = 0, contradicting charge accumulation on capacitor plates.
Substituting Gauss law rho = eps0 div E makes the total effective current J + Jd strictly divergence-free everywhere, so all spanning surfaces give identical flux.
Worked check (Q17): if signed electric flux grows at 4.00e8 V m/s across a fixed vacuum surface, Id = (8.85e-12)(4.00e8) = 3.54 mA.

cards.title: Capacitor identities: Id = dq/dt = C dV/dt
items: In the quasistatic parallel-plate model (plate separation d << radius a, variation time tau >> a/c), E = q/(eps0 A) is uniform across area A, so Phi_E = E A = q/eps0.
Displacement current has the SI unit ampere and generates the exact same magnetic field as conduction current, even though no electrons cross the vacuum gap.
For AC drive V(t) = V0 sin(wt), electric flux and voltage peak at wt = pi/2 while Id = w C V0 cos(wt) peaks at wt = 0: Id leads V by 90 deg.

cards.title: Steady DC, discharge & sign rules
items: Link loop traversal and surface normal by the right-hand curl rule: if fingers curl along C, thumb sets the positive normal for BOTH conduction and displacement flux.
During capacitor discharge through a resistor, E decreases while E still points from + to - plate, so dPhi_E/dt < 0 reverses B alongside reversing wire current.
For moving plates at constant charge q, E = q/(eps0 A) stays fixed so Id = 0, even though plate voltage V = E d(t) is changing!

title: Capacitor gap magnetic field & dielectrics
subtitle: Radial profile of B_phi inside and outside circular plates, rim continuity check, and bound polarisation current in matter.
takeaway: Inside circular plates B_phi rises linearly with r and peaks at rim r = a; in a dielectric, A dD/dt = Ic splits into vacuum + bound parts.
source: Source: electromagnetic-waves/Electromagnetic-waves.md sec. 2.2, C2, E1, E2, Q2, Q9, Q18

cards.title: Azimuthal B_phi inside and outside circular plates
items: For circular plates of radius a carrying charging current Ic, a coaxial circle of radius r < a encloses fraction (pi r^2)/(pi a^2) = r^2/a^2 of the uniform gap flux.
B_\phi(r)=\frac{\mu_0 I_c r}{2\pi a^2}\ (r\leqslant a), \qquad B_\phi(r)=\frac{\mu_0 I_c}{2\pi r}\ (r\geqslant a)
Plate spacing d cancels completely! On the symmetry axis r = 0 so B = 0; at rim r = a both formulas match cleanly at B_max = mu0 Ic / (2 pi a).
Worked exemplar (E1): a = 0.050 m, Ic = 0.020 A gives B(0.02 m) = 32 nT, rim peak B(0.05 m) = 80 nT, and outside B(0.10 m) = 40 nT.

cards.title: Macroscopic displacement current in a dielectric
items: Fill the capacitor uniformly with linear nonmagnetic dielectric eps = kappa eps0. Free plate charge q_f sets D = q_f / A = eps0 E + P_pol across the gap.
Bound charges shift locally inside molecules, creating genuine polarisation current A dP_pol/dt without free electrons crossing the insulator.
Worked split (E2): kappa = 5 at Ic = 15 mA gives total A dD/dt = 15 mA, split into 3 mA vacuum term + 12 mA polarisation current (sum = 15 mA).

cards.title: Fixed-Ic vs fixed-(dV/dt) constraint trap
items: Always check which variable the external circuit holds constant when comparing an empty capacitor to one filled with dielectric constant kappa (C2, Q2):
At fixed current source Ic, dD/dt = Ic/A does not change so B_phi is untouched (dE/dt drops by kappa). At fixed voltage ramp dV/dt, current scales by kappa.
Never write eps0 A dE/dt = Ic inside a kappa > 1 dielectric: eps0 A dE/dt is only Ic / kappa, missing fraction (1 - 1/kappa) carried by bound charges (Q9).

cards.title: Leaky resistor-capacitor & validity limits
items: If an Ohmic medium of conductivity sigma and permittivity eps fills the gap under voltage V(t), free conduction current J_f = sigma E and displacement J_d = eps dE/dt coexist:
At low frequencies (w << sigma/eps) conduction dominates; above relaxation frequency w_c = sigma/eps, displacement current wins.
Quasistatic formula B_phi = mu0 Ic r/(2 pi a^2) assumes w a << c; at microwave frequencies radial wave variations replace uniform E(t) by Bessel modes.

title: All four Maxwell equations in vacuum & matter
subtitle: Integral and differential forms side by side, physical meaning of each law, and linear constitutive relations.
takeaway: Maxwell unites two divergence laws (sources) with two coupled curl laws (time-varying fields); no magnetic monopoles exist (div B = 0).

cards.title: Microscopic (vacuum) Maxwell equations
items: Every classical electromagnetic phenomenon in vacuum is governed by four coupled field laws linking total charge density rho and total current density J:
Gauss theorem turns div laws into closed-surface fluxes; Stokes theorem turns curl laws into line integrals around fixed loop boundaries.

cards.title: Macroscopic laws in matter: separate free sources
items: Absorbing bound charge into D = eps0 E + P and bound currents into H = B/mu0 - M isolates controllable free charge rho_f and free current J_f:
Notice asymmetry: magnetic Gauss law keeps B (never H, since div H = -div M != 0 at pole faces), while Faraday keeps E and B unmodified.

cards.title: Model L constitutive closure & SI constants
items: A homogeneous, isotropic, linear, lossless, nondispersive medium (Model L) closes Maxwell equations with positive constants eps = eps_r eps0 and mu = mu_r mu0:
Check SI constants: eps0 = 8.85e-12 F/m, mu0 = 4 pi e-7 H/m give Z0 = sqrt(mu0/eps0) = 376.7 Ohm ~ 377 Ohm and 1/sqrt(mu0 eps0) = 2.998e8 m/s.
Do not plug DC dielectric constant kappa_static (e.g. water ~ 80) into optical index n ~ 1.33: heavy dipoles freeze out at optical frequencies!

cards.title: Symmetry, causality & moving-loop warning
items: In a travelling wave, "changing E creates B and changing B creates E" is only a verbal mnemonic — not a time lag! Both curls hold simultaneously at each (r, t).
In source-free space (rho_f = 0, J_f = 0), E and B become symmetric up to duality E -> v B, B -> -E/v, unlocking self-sustaining wave propagation.
Fixed-loop integral curl E = -dB/dt gives only transformer EMF; if wire segments move at velocity u through B, include u x B motional EMF separately.

title: Curl-curl derivations, wave speed & refraction
subtitle: Deriving both vector wave equations, why charge-free homogeneity is essential, and wavelength vs frequency in matter.
takeaway: Wave speed is v = c / sqrt(mu_r eps_r); stationary boundaries keep frequency f strictly constant while scaling lambda = lambda_0 / n.
source: Source: electromagnetic-waves/Electromagnetic-waves.md sec. 2.4, C3, E3, Q3, Q10, Q19

cards.title: Deriving both 3D vector wave equations
items: In homogeneous source-free Model L (rho_f = 0, J_f = 0, constant eps and mu), take the curl of Faraday law and substitute curl B = mu eps dE/dt:
Charge-free constant eps forces div E = 0, killing grad(div E); div B = 0 kills grad(div B) identically in the parallel curl-of-Ampere derivation.

cards.title: Phase speed & refractive index in matter
items: Substitute any plane waveform F(z - v t): d^2F/dz^2 = F" and d^2F/dt^2 = v^2 F", forcing mu eps v^2 = 1. Compare with vacuum c = 1/sqrt(mu0 eps0):
Quick checks: if eps_r = 4 and mu_r = 9 (Q3), n = sqrt(36) = 6 so v = c/6 (never omit mu_r or the square root!). Nonmagnetic matter has mu_r = 1 so n = sqrt(eps_r).
Dimensional check: [mu0 eps0] = (N A^-2)(C^2 N^-1 m^-2) = C^2/(A^2 m^2) = s^2/m^2, so [1/sqrt(mu0 eps0)] = m/s automatically!

cards.title: Refraction: frequency stays fixed, wavelength shrinks
items: Boundary fields at a stationary interface must match at EVERY instant t, forcing exp(-i w t) to carry identical angular frequency w in both media (E3, Q19):
Worked exemplar (E3): f = 6.00e14 Hz (lambda_0 = 500 nm green) enters nonmagnetic glass eps_r = 2.25 (n = 1.50): v = 2.00e8 m/s, lambda = 333 nm, colour stays 600 THz!
Never classify a wave inside glass with lambda = 333 nm as "ultraviolet": spectral bands and photon energy E = h f depend on f (or vacuum lambda_0), never lambda_med.

cards.title: Hidden coupling & inhomogeneous-medium trap
items: Six scalar components (Ex, Ey, Ez, Bx, By, Bz) each satisfy the wave equation, yet you CANNOT pick them independently (Q10):
In graded-index fibres (eps = eps(r)), div E != 0 restores the extra grad(div E) term so simple decoupled wave equations fail (C3).
Even in vacuum, Ex = E0 sin(kx - wt) is ILLEGAL because div E = dEx/dx = k E0 cos(kx - wt) != 0 violates Gauss law in charge-free space!

title: Plane-wave kinematics, phase & right-handed triad
subtitle: Reading k and w with correct signs, reconstructing B from E without sign mistakes, and testing valid Maxwell fields.
takeaway: Read direction k_hat from constant phase first, verify k . E = 0, then compute B = (k_hat x E) / v; never use c when v = c / n.
source: Source: electromagnetic-waves/Electromagnetic-waves.md sec. 2.5, C4, E4, Q4, Q11, Q20, Q30

cards.title: Reading propagation vector k & speed from phase
items: Set phase phi(r, t) = k . r - w t = constant (or w t - k . r = constant): differentiating gives k . dr/dt = w, so crests move along +k_hat at speed v = w/|k|.
\phi = k_x x + k_y y + k_z z \mp \omega t \Rightarrow \hat{\mathbf{k}} = \pm\frac{(k_x, k_y, k_z)}{\sqrt{k_x^2 + k_y^2 + k_z^2}}
Opposite signs on space and time (kz - wt or wt - kz) mean travel in +z; SAME signs (kz + wt) mean travel in -z! Always check sign first.
Standard links: k = 2 pi / lambda, w = 2 pi f, T = 1/f, and v = w / k = f lambda = c / sqrt(mu_r eps_r).

cards.title: Transversality & exact vector link B = (k_hat x E)/v
items: Apply nabla -> i k to all four source-free Maxwell equations for a single monochromatic plane wave in homogeneous Model L:
(E_hat, B_hat, k_hat) form a right-handed orthonormal triad at every instant: E x B always points along +k_hat because real factor 1/v > 0 keeps E and B in phase!
In a dielectric of index n > 1, E0 = v B0 = (c/n) B0 (Q11, Q30): blindly writing B0 = E0 / c underestimates magnetic amplitude by factor n!

cards.title: Worked vector reconstructions without guesswork
items: Exemplar E4: in vacuum E = 60 cos(2z - 6.00e8 t) x_hat (SI). Here k = +2 z_hat, w = 6.00e8 rad/s -> v = w/k = 3.00e8 m/s = c along +z_hat.
Cross-product drill (C4, Q4): if wave moves along -x_hat and E points along +z_hat, B_hat = (-x_hat) x (+z_hat) = +y_hat. Verify: E_hat x B_hat = z x y = -x_hat!
Half a cycle later both E and B flip sign simultaneously (-E) x (-B) = +(E x B), so energy continues flowing along -x_hat without reversal.

cards.title: Four-step validity test for candidate exam fields
items: JEE Advanced frequently offers 4 vector expressions and asks which represents a valid plane EM wave in charge-free space. Test in exact order:
Any failure in steps 1-4 disqualifies the candidate immediately. E.g. E = E0 sin(kx - wt) (x_hat + y_hat) has k = k x_hat, so k . E0 = k E0 != 0 -> INVALID!
For tilted wave vector k = 3 x_hat + 4 y_hat, orthogonality means 3 Ex + 4 Ey = 0, so E0 proportional to (4 x_hat - 3 y_hat) IS valid!

title: Polarisation states, unpolarised light & Malus law
subtitle: Superposing orthogonal transverse modes, linear/circular/elliptical criteria, and polaroid analyser chains.
takeaway: Polarisation tracks the transverse E vector; unpolarised light transmits I0/2 through the first ideal polariser and I_prev cos^2(theta) thereafter.
source: Source: electromagnetic-waves/Electromagnetic-waves.md sec. 2.6 + polaroid bridge to Wave Optics

cards.title: Linear, circular & elliptical polarisation criteria
items: Superpose two orthogonal transverse plane waves propagating along +z with phase difference delta (where phi = kz - wt):
Case 1: delta = m pi -> straight line of slope (-1)^m E_0y/E_0x (linear). Case 2: E_0x = E_0y and delta = +-pi/2 -> circle Ex^2 + Ey^2 = E0^2. All others -> ellipse.
Even for circular/elliptical waves, instantaneous B = (z_hat x E)/v still has |B| = |E|/v and stays perpendicular to E at every instant!

cards.title: Unpolarised light & Malus cos^2(theta) law
items: Natural thermal/lamp light consists of rapid random jumps in phase delta, sweeping all transverse directions equally: <cos^2(theta)> = 1/2.
An ideal linear polaroid projects electric amplitude onto pass axis p_hat: E_trans = E_in cos(theta), and squaring field amplitude gives cos^2(theta) in intensity.
Measure theta between consecutive polaroid pass axes (or between incoming E direction and pass axis) — if a problem states angle to the block axis, use sin^2!

cards.title: Crossed polaroids + rotating middle sheet
items: Place two crossed polaroids P1 (0 deg) and P3 (90 deg), then insert middle polaroid P2 at angle theta to P1 for incident unpolarised intensity I0:
At theta = 45 deg, I_out peaks at I0 / 8 (non-zero even though P1 and P3 are orthogonal!) because P2 projects a fresh component along 45 deg.
Rotation check: in one full 2 pi revolution of P2, sin^2(2 theta) hits 4 maxima (at 45, 135, 225, 315 deg) and 4 zeros (0, 90, 180, 270 deg).

cards.title: Circular-wave intensity & near-field warning
items: Compare a linearly polarised wave E = E0 cos(phi) x_hat against a circularly polarised wave E = E_c (cos(phi) x_hat + sin(phi) y_hat) of constant magnitude E_c:
In circular polarisation |E(t)| = E_c is constant in time (never drops to zero!), so mean energy density is eps E_c^2 without the 1/2 factor!
Longitudinal E components DO exist inside waveguided TM modes, plasma oscillations, and electrostatic near fields — just never in a vacuum plane wave.

title: Field energy density & Poynting theorem
subtitle: Stored electric/magnetic energy densities, exact curl derivation of energy flux S = E x H, and travelling-wave equipartition.
takeaway: In a single travelling plane wave uE = uB at EVERY instant (both peak and vanish together), giving S = (E x B)/mu = u v k_hat.

cards.title: Electric & magnetic energy densities
items: From parallel-plate storage U = (1/2) C V^2 / (A d) and solenoid storage U = (1/2) L I^2 / (A l), linear nondispersive media store local field energy density:
u_E = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon E^2, \qquad u_B = \frac{B^2}{2\mu}, \qquad u = u_E + u_B
Both terms have SI dimensions J/m^3 = N/m^2 = Pa (identical dimensions to pressure!). Total field energy in volume V is integral of u dV.
Do not apply u = (1/2) eps E^2 blindly inside ferromagnetic hysteresis loops or strongly dispersive media near resonances where d(w eps)/dw enters.

cards.title: Poynting vector & exact local conservation law
items: Apply vector identity div(E x H) = H . (curl E) - E . (curl H) and substitute Faraday + Maxwell-Ampere laws for constant real eps, mu:
Integrating over fixed volume V says: rate of loss of stored EM energy (-dU/dt) equals outward power flux oint S . dA PLUS mechanical/Ohmic power J_f . E on charges.
Units check: [E][H] = (V/m)(A/m) = W/m^2 (power per unit area normal to S). In a DC wire carrying I across voltage V, radial S feeds I^2 R heat from outside!

cards.title: Instantaneous equipartition in a single plane wave
items: Substitute B = E / v and v^-2 = mu eps into uB for one travelling plane wave in homogeneous source-free Model L (Q11):
u_B = \frac{(E/v)^2}{2\mu} = \frac{\mu\varepsilon E^2}{2\mu} = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon E^2 = u_E \Rightarrow u = \varepsilon E^2 = \frac{B^2}{\mu}
Unlike an LC circuit or standing string where kinetic/magnetic peak when potential/electric is zero, a travelling wave carries uE and uB IN PHASE at every (r, t)!
Equipartition uE = uB holds for ONE travelling wave, NOT for static fields, near fields, or standing waves (where E nodes sit at B antinodes!).

cards.title: Transport velocity link: S = u v k_hat
items: Combine |S| = E B / mu = E^2 / (mu v) with total density u = eps E^2 and mu eps = 1/v^2 for any single plane wave waveform f(kz - wt):
In time dt, a cylinder of base area A and length v dt sweeps all energy inside volume A (v dt) across surface A: dU = u A v dt -> flux S = dU/(A dt) = u v.
Averaging over one period preserves the exact transport identity: mean intensity I = <S> = v <u> (in vacuum: I = c <u>, so <u> = I / c).

title: Peak vs RMS amplitude, impedance & 1/r^2 scaling
subtitle: All six equivalent intensity expressions, vacuum impedance Z0 = 377 Ohm, and point-source vs collimated beam scaling.
takeaway: I = E0^2/(2Z) = E_rms^2/Z = v <u>; for an isotropic point source I ~ 1/r^2 so E0 and B0 drop as 1/r, whereas a collimated laser keeps I constant.
source: Source: electromagnetic-waves/Electromagnetic-waves.md sec. 2.8, C5, E5, Q5, Q21, Q22, Q32

cards.title: All equivalent intensity formulas in one chain
items: Define wave impedance Z = E/H = mu v = sqrt(mu/eps) = Z0 sqrt(mu_r/eps_r). Since <sin^2(phi)> = 1/2, E_rms = E0/sqrt(2) and B_rms = B0/sqrt(2):
I = \langle S\rangle = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon v E_0^2 = \frac{E_0 B_0}{2\mu} = \frac{v B_0^2}{2\mu} = \frac{E_0^2}{2 Z} = \frac{E_{\mathrm{rms}}^2}{Z} = v\langle u\rangle
Notice how Z unifies electricity and optics: I = E_rms^2 / Z mirrors resistor power V_rms^2 / R with Z0 = 377 Ohm in vacuum (Z = Z0 / n if mu_r = 1).
Never average before multiplying (C5, Q12): <E> = 0 and <B> = 0, yet <E x B> = (E0 B0 / 2) k_hat > 0 because E and B reverse together every half-period!

cards.title: Worked peak vs RMS & energy-density drills
items: Exemplar E5: vacuum linear wave with peak E0 = 120 V/m has I = 0.5 * (8.85e-12)(3.0e8)(120)^2 = 19.1 W/m^2, <u> = I/c = 63.7 nJ/m^3, <uE> = 31.9 nJ/m^3.

\langle u\rangle = \varepsilon E_{\mathrm{rms}}^2 = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon E_0^2, \qquad \langle u_E\rangle = \langle u_B\rangle = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon E_{\mathrm{rms}}^2 = \frac{1}{4}\varepsilon E_0^2
Paper checks (Q5, Q21, Q22): E_rms = 30.0 V/m in vacuum gives I = 30^2 / 377 = 2.39 W/m^2 (NO extra 1/2!). Beam I = 240 W/m^2 gives <u> = 240 / 3e8 = 0.800 uJ/m^3.
#1 exam error: inserting an extra 1/2 into E_rms^2 / Z0 or forgetting 1/2 in eps0 c E0^2 / 2! Always circle whether question data gives PEAK or RMS!

cards.title: Point source vs line source vs collimated laser
items: Energy conservation across enclosing surfaces in lossless space fixes how intensity I and peak amplitude E0 scale with distance r:
\mathrm{Point:}\ I=\frac{\mathcal{P}}{4\pi r^2}\ (E_0\propto r^{-1});\ \ \mathrm{Line:}\ I=\frac{\mathcal{P}}{2\pi r L}\ (E_0\propto r^{-1/2})
Worked beacon (Q32): P = 120 W isotropic at r = 3.00 m gives I = 120/(36 pi) = 1.061 W/m^2, E0 = sqrt(2 I Z0) = 28.3 V/m, B0 = E0/c = 94.2 nT.
For an ideal parallel laser beam of cross-section pi w^2, I = P/(pi w^2) and E0 remain independent of distance r (neglecting diffraction).

cards.title: Lamp efficiency & photon-flux bridge
items: If a bulb of electrical input P_elec converts fraction eta to monochromatic radiation of wavelength lambda_0 isotropically, photon flux phi_ph (photons / m^2 s) at distance r is:
I(r) = \frac{\eta \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{elec}}}{4\pi r^2}, \qquad \Phi_{\mathrm{photon}} = \frac{I(r)}{h c / \lambda_0} = \frac{\eta \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{elec}} \lambda_0}{4\pi r^2 h c}
Links classical Maxwell wave amplitude E0 = sqrt(2 I Z0) directly to quantum counting rate N_dot = Phi_photon A_det cos(theta) on a detector.
If light reflects off a plane mirror behind the point source, add the image source at image distance r_img (coherent phase if laser, intensities if thermal)!

title: Field momentum & flat-surface radiation pressure
subtitle: Maxwell momentum density g = S/c^2, why cos^2(theta) appears for tilted plates, tangential shear force, and partial reflection.
takeaway: Actual flat area A_s at angle theta feels normal pressure P_n = (1+R)(I/c)cos^2(theta) and shear (1-R)(I/c)sin(theta)cos(theta); if P_hit is given, drop ONE cosine!
source: Source: electromagnetic-waves/Electromagnetic-waves.md sec. 2.9-2.10, C6, E6, E7, Q6, Q12, Q13, Q23-Q25, Q33

cards.title: Field momentum density & pulse impulse
items: Combining Lorentz force density rho E + J x B with Maxwell stress tensor T_ij in vacuum identifies electromagnetic momentum density g and collimated pulse momentum p:
Pulse impulse (E6, Q23): a collimated 9.00 mJ pulse hitting a flat mirror normally reverses momentum +U/c -> -U/c, delivering J = 2 U/c = 6.00e-11 N s (absorber: 3.00e-11 N s).
Isotropic or counter-propagating equal beams have total energy U > 0 yet net vector momentum p = 0 (Q12): p = U/c holds ONLY for unidirectional vacuum radiation!

cards.title: Flat oblique surface: why TWO cosines appear
items: Let uniform vacuum beam of intensity I strike flat area A_s at angle theta to surface normal n_hat. Energy hitting patch in dt is dU = I (A_s cos theta) dt:
First cos(theta) shrinks intercepted beam cross-section; second cos(theta) projects normal momentum (1 + R)(dU/c)cos(theta). Dividing by actual area A_s gives cos^2(theta)!
CRITICAL TRAP (C6, Q25): if a question ALREADY gives intercepted power P_hit (e.g. 12 W beam all landing on a 60 deg mirror), area projection is DONE: F_n = 2(P_hit/c)cos(theta) = 40 nN!

cards.title: Tangential shear traction & transparent sheets
items: Decompose incident ray unit vector k_hat = cos(theta) n_hat + sin(theta) t_hat (inward normal n_hat, surface tangent t_hat). Specular rays keep tangential momentum unchanged, absorbed rays transfer it all (Q13, Q33):
F_n = (1 + R - T)\frac{I A_s}{c}\cos^2\theta, \qquad F_t = \mathcal{A}\frac{I A_s}{c}\sin\theta\cos\theta
For a pure absorber (A = 1, R = T = 0), sqrt(F_n^2 + F_t^2) = I A_s cos(theta)/c points straight along incoming beam k_hat, NOT normal to the plate!

cards.title: Emissive recoil & laser levitation balance
items: A horizontal mirror disc of mass m levitates atop a vertical upward laser beam of total power P_beam (all hitting disc, normal incidence R = 1) when:
Because c = 3e8 m/s is huge, levitating just m = 1 mg requires P = 0.5 * 1e-6 * 9.8 * 3e8 = 1.47 kW of continuous reflected optical power!
If a black plate heats up and re-radiates equally from BOTH faces, thermal emission recoils cancel; if insulated on one back face, isotropic emission adds recoil!

title: Electromagnetic spectrum, sources & applications
subtitle: Adopted classroom wavelength cutoffs, physical emission mechanisms, RADAR ranging, and origin-overlap traps.
takeaway: All bands obey c = f lambda_0 in vacuum; X-ray vs gamma-ray naming follows physical origin (electronic vs nuclear), so their energies overlap.
source: Source: electromagnetic-waves/Electromagnetic-waves.md sec. 2.12, E9, E10, Q7, Q8, Q15, Q27, Q28, Q35

cards.title: Seven spectral bands & six memorisable cutoffs
items: In decreasing vacuum wavelength lambda_0 (increasing frequency f = c/lambda_0 and photon energy E_gamma = h f = 1240 eV nm / lambda_0):
Corresponding frequencies are 300 MHz, 300 GHz, 429 THz, 750 THz, 30 PHz, and 30 EHz. Quick microwave rule: f(GHz) * lambda_0(cm) = 30 (2.4 GHz -> 12.5 cm, Q7)!
Band boundaries are human conventions, NOT sudden changes in Maxwell laws; all seven travel at identical speed c = 299,792,458 m/s in vacuum (Q8).

cards.title: Production mechanisms (NCERT + JEE Main/Adv core)
items: Match every band to its primary physical generator: Radio = accelerated charges in conducting antennas / LC circuits; Microwave = klystron, magnetron, Gunn diode.
Infrared = hot bodies & molecular vibrational-rotational transitions; Visible = outer valence electronic jumps; UV = inner valence jumps, mercury lamps, excimer lasers (193 nm LASIK, Q15).
Origin test (E10): a 100 keV photon (lambda_0 = 0.0124 nm) emitted by a decelerating electron is an X-ray; the exact same 100 keV photon from a nucleus is a gamma ray!

cards.title: RADAR echo ranging, greenhouse & microwave heating
items: A pulse emitted at t = 0 reflects off a target at range r and returns after echo delay dt: total path traveled by the wave is 2 r, NOT r (E9, Q27, Q35):
Worked numbers: dt = 8.00 us gives r = 1200 m (Q27); KrF UV laser at 248 nm has E_gamma = 1240/248 = 5.00 eV (Q28); Cu-target X-ray at 0.100 nm has 12.4 keV (Q35).
Microwave ovens drive polar water molecules via oscillating E torques (dielectric loss, NOT simple sharp gas-phase resonance); greenhouse gases absorb/re-emit thermal IR (~10 um).

cards.title: Atmospheric windows, ozone & ionospheric reflection
items: Stratospheric ozone O3 absorbs solar UV-B/C (~200-310 nm), protecting life; ordinary glass transmits visible light but blocks most thermal IR and short UV.
Shortwave HF skywaves (~3-30 MHz) undergo total internal reflection off ionospheric free electrons, whereas VHF/TV/microwaves (> 40 MHz) pierce straight through to satellites!
Do not claim "thermal bodies emit ONLY infrared": hot filaments and the 5800 K Sun emit thermal radiation peaking in the visible while spanning IR through UV!

title: LC oscillators, accelerating charges & dipole antennas
subtitle: Why acceleration is required for radiation, Hertzian dipole angular pattern sin^2(theta), and w^4 Rayleigh/antenna scaling.
takeaway: Stationary charges give E ~ 1/r^2, steady currents give B ~ 1/r^2; ONLY accelerating charges produce 1/r fields that carry power to infinity.

cards.title: Lumped LC tank vs open radiating dipole
items: In an ideal closed LC circuit, Kirchhoff loop balance L d^2q/dt^2 + q/C = 0 sets the oscillation frequency of the carrier wave:
Opening the capacitor plates out into a straight half-wave rod of length L_ant ~ lambda_0 / 2 lets oscillating fields detach into space efficiently instead of staying trapped.
A sub-wavelength loop/rod of size d << lambda_0 is a terrible radiator unless matched: efficient dipole antennas use L_ant = lambda_0 / 2 or quarter-wave monopole lambda_0 / 4!

cards.title: Why ONLY accelerated charges radiate energy
items: Integrate Poynting flux over a sphere of huge radius r -> infinity: surface area grows as 4 pi r^2, so nonzero total power P_rad requires S ~ 1/r^2 and hence |E|, |B| ~ 1/r:
E_{\mathrm{stat}}\propto r^{-2}\Rightarrow S\propto r^{-4}\to 0;\qquad E_{\mathrm{rad}}\propto \frac{q a_\perp}{r}\Rightarrow P_{\mathrm{rad}}>0
A charge moving at constant velocity v carries its convective field along with it without shedding energy (verified immediately by jumping to its rest frame!).
Larmor power formula for a single non-relativistic point charge q with acceleration a: P_rad = mu0 q^2 a^2 / (6 pi c).

cards.title: Hertzian oscillating electric dipole pattern
items: For a short dipole p(t) = p0 cos(wt) z_hat along the z-axis (size d << lambda << r), far-field intensity depends on polar angle theta from z_hat and frequency w:
Along the dipole axis (theta = 0 or pi), accelerated charges move purely radially toward the observer, so transverse projection a_perp = a sin(theta) vanishes: ZERO axial radiation!
Polarisation check: far-field E lies along polar unit vector theta_hat (in the plane containing z_hat and r_hat), while B wraps azimuthally along phi_hat.

cards.title: Blue sky & red sunset: the w^4 Rayleigh bridge
items: Sunlight drives bound electrons in atmospheric molecules as tiny induced dipoles p0 = alpha E_inc. Since P_scat ~ w^4 ~ lambda_0^-4:
Short blue/violet wavelengths scatter ~6-9x more strongly sidewards (blue sky), leaving direct long-path sunset beams enriched in unscattered red/orange light.
Notice directional ratio for dipole vs isotropic: since <sin^2(theta)>_sphere = 2/3, peak equatorial intensity I_max(theta = 90 deg) = (3/2) * P_tot / (4 pi r^2)!

title: EM waves master triage, scales & examiner traps
subtitle: Complete 6-branch problem playbook, mental-math constants, and the ten highest-frequency JEE Advanced traps.
takeaway: Before substituting numbers, write four tags on paper: [medium n, Z], [PEAK vs RMS], [k_hat sign], and [beam-normal A vs tilted A_s].

cards.title: Fast mental-arithmetic constants for exams
items: Keep six pre-combined combinations ready so you never multiply raw powers of 8.85e-12 and 4 pi e-7 under time pressure:
Look how instant E5 becomes with Z0 = 120 pi: for E0 = 120 V/m, I = 120^2 / (2 * 120 pi) = 60 / pi = 19.10 W/m^2 in three seconds flat!

cards.title: Top amplitude & wave-equation traps
items: Peak vs RMS factor of 2: I = E0^2 / (2 Z) = E_rms^2 / Z, and <u> = (1/2) eps E0^2 = eps E_rms^2. Confusing the two drops half the marks on numericals.
Medium ratio E0 = v B0: in water/glass of index n, B0 = n E0 / c, NOT E0 / c!
Divergence test: F(kx - wt) solves the 1D wave PDE, yet E = F(kx - wt) x_hat is NOT an EM wave in free space because k . E != 0!
Coherent superposition: add vector fields E_tot = E1 + E2 BEFORE squaring; never add intensities directly when two coherent beams interfere or form a standing wave!

cards.title: Top force, cosine & surface traps
items: Cosine count: given intensity I on tilted area A_s -> F_n = (1+R)(I A_s/c)cos^2(theta). Given total beam power P_hit landing on tilted mirror -> F_n = 2(P_hit/c)cos(theta)!
Absorber direction: a tilted black plate feels force straight along incident beam k_hat (both normal P_n and shear F_t != 0), NOT perpendicular to the plate!
Polished sphere vs flat mirror: both black sphere AND specular sphere feel F = I pi a^2 / c; only a flat normal mirror feels 2 I pi a^2 / c!
Transparent plate: use P_n = (1 + R - T)(I/c)cos^2(theta), NEVER (1 + R)I/c when transmitted fraction T > 0 carries forward momentum away!

cards.title: Five-step pre-submission check protocol
items: 1. Spanning surface check: did you evaluate Ic and Id on ONE surface bounded by C, respecting fixed-I vs fixed-dV/dt constraints?
2. Triad check: did you test k . E = 0 and verify E_hat x B_hat points along the sign of constant phase (+k_hat)?
3. Limiting check: does P_n vanish as theta -> 90 deg, recover I/c at R = 0, and double to 2I/c at R = 1?

title: Radial Poynting flux in capacitors, wires & coax
subtitle: How circuits truly transport energy through empty space around wires, exact Q29 gap flux proof, and coaxial TEM guides.
takeaway: Wires guide fields, while energy travels in the surrounding space via S = E x H: inward into capacitors/resistors and axially along coax.

cards.title: Charging capacitor: inward radial energy flux (Q29)
items: Take circular vacuum plates of radius a, spacing d << a, E = E z_hat and azimuthal B_phi(a) = mu0 Ic / (2 pi a) phi_hat at cylindrical rim r = a:
Notice z_hat x phi_hat = -r_hat! Electrostatic energy stored in the gap enters sideways from the surrounding field across the rim area 2 pi a d.

cards.title: Cylindrical Ohmic wire: radial inflow feeds Joule heat
items: A steady DC current I runs along +z through a cylindrical wire of radius a, length l, resistance R = V/I: inside E = (V/l) z_hat and surface B_phi(a) = mu0 I/(2 pi a):
\mathbf{S}(a) = -\frac{V I}{2\pi a \ell}\,\hat{\mathbf{r}} \Rightarrow \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{in}} = |\mathbf{S}(a)|(2\pi a \ell) = V I = I^2 R
Battery fields outside the metal funnel energy radially inward through the wire surface at rate I^2 R, where collisions convert it into lattice heat!
Inside radius r < a, E(r) = V/l is uniform while B_phi(r) ~ r, so inward power across radius r is V I (r^2/a^2) — proportional to enclosed volume!

cards.title: Coaxial cable: lossless TEM wave power transport
items: Inner core radius a (+I along +z, potential +V) and outer shield radius b (-I, potential 0) carry radial E_r and azimuthal B_phi in insulator (eps, mu):
E_r = \frac{V}{r\ln(b/a)}, \qquad B_\phi = \frac{\mu I}{2\pi r}, \qquad S_z = \frac{V I}{2\pi r^2\ln(b/a)}
Integrating S_z across the annular dielectric gives exact circuit power V I! For vacuum coax, Z_coax = 60 ln(b/a) Ohm (50 Ohm standard at b/a = 2.30).

cards.title: Hidden magnetic-energy term & validity fence
items: In Q29 with non-steady current q(t) = alpha t^2 (Ic = 2 alpha t), changing B_phi inside the gap induces a small second-order radial correction to E(r):
U_B = \int_0^a \frac{B_\phi^2}{2\mu_0}\,2\pi r d\,dr = \frac{\mu_0 I_c^2 d}{16\pi}, \qquad \frac{U_B}{U_E} \sim \left(\frac{\omega a}{c}\right)^2
When variation time tau >> a/c (w a << c), U_B << U_E justifies Model Q. Retention of dU_B/dt gives the next term in the cylindrical cavity expansion!
Never extrapolate quasistatic gap fields to t -> 0 shock steps where dI/dt is impulsive: sharp wavefronts travel radially inward at speed c!

title: Curved-surface forces, cones & stellar beta blow-out
subtitle: Exact integrals proving F_black = F_specular = I pi a^2/c on a sphere, cone/cylinder drag factors, and astrophysical radiation blow-out.
takeaway: A specular sphere scatters light into all directions with <cos(2 theta)> = 0, feeling the EXACT same force I pi a^2 / c as a black sphere!
source: Source: electromagnetic-waves/Electromagnetic-waves.md sec. 2.11, E8, Q14, Q26, Q34

cards.title: Why black & specular spheres feel identical axial force
items: Divide the sunlit hemisphere of radius a >> lambda into ring zones dA = 2 pi a^2 sin(theta) d(theta) at normal angle theta in [0, pi/2] (sec. 2.11, Q14):
Physical miracle: a ray hitting at theta scatters at angle pi - 2 theta from forward, carrying away axial momentum -(dU/c)cos(2 theta) whose hemisphere average vanishes!

cards.title: Cones, cylinders & retroreflectors compared
items: Apply the exact same local vector projection dF_z = dF_n cos(theta) + dF_t sin(theta) across other symmetric bodies of projected cross-section A_proj:

Here alpha_0 is the cone semi-vertical angle (normal makes theta = pi/2 - alpha_0 with axis). Check limits: alpha_0 = pi/2 (flat disc) -> (1 + R) I pi a^2 / c; sharp needle alpha_0 -> 0 with R = 1 -> 0!
Specular circular cylinder of radius a, length L perpendicular to beam: int_{-pi/2}^{pi/2} 2 cos^3(theta) d(theta) = 8/3 -> F = (4/3)(2 I a L / c) vs black 2 I a L / c!

cards.title: Stellar radiation blow-out ratio beta (Q34)
items: Around a star of luminosity L_* and mass M_*, compare outward radiation force I pi a^2/c on a spherical dust grain (density rho_m, radius a) to inward gravity G M_* m / r^2:
\beta \equiv \frac{F_{\mathrm{rad}}}{F_{\mathrm{grav}}} = \frac{3 L_\star}{16\pi c G M_\star \rho_m a}, \qquad a_{\mathrm{crit}}(\beta=1) = \frac{3 L_\star}{16\pi c G M_\star \rho_m}
Both I = L_*/(4 pi r^2) and gravity fall strictly as 1/r^2, so orbital distance r CANCELS COMPLETELY! For Sun (L_sun = 3.83e26 W, M_sun = 1.99e30 kg) & silicates, a_crit ~ 0.2 um.
Do not let beta -> infinity as a -> 0: once grain radius a ~ lambda (~0.5 um), geometric optics breaks down and Mie/Rayleigh scattering cross-section drops as a^6!

cards.title: Lambertian diffuse reflector: third classic case
items: If an opaque flat disc (projected normal incidence) re-scatters all incident energy diffusely with Lambert cosine radiance (~ cos psi into hemisphere), outgoing normal momentum adds 2/3:
Diffuse bounce always sits strictly between total absorption (1 * I/c) and normal specular mirror (2 * I/c) because oblique scattered rays waste sideways momentum.
Exemplar check (E8): a = 1.00 mm grain, rho_m = 3000 kg/m^3 at I = 1200 W/m^2 gives F = 12.6 pN and a = 3 I/(4 rho_m a c) = 1.00e-6 m/s^2.

title: Wave impedance, Fresnel matching & quarter-wave coats
subtitle: Boundary loops for tangential E and H, why t_E > 1 never violates energy conservation, and impedance-matching layers.
takeaway: Reflection is governed by wave impedance Z = sqrt(mu/eps), NOT refractive index n alone; always compute power transmission as T = (Z1/Z2) t_E^2.

cards.title: Tangential boundary equations & reflected H sign
items: Shrink rectangular Faraday and Ampere loops across a charge/current-free planar interface z = 0 between lossless media Z1 (z < 0) and Z2 (z > 0):
Keeping +x_hat for E_i, E_r, E_t means forward wave has H_i = +E_i/Z1 y_hat, while reflected wave moving along -z_hat has H_r = -E_r/Z1 y_hat!

cards.title: Energy conservation & the "t_E > 1" paradox (Q16, Q36)
items: Intensity is I = E0^2 / (2 Z), so transmitted intensity carries factor 1/Z2 while incident carries 1/Z1. Dividing I_r and I_t by I_i proves exact flux balance:
R = r_E^2 = \left(\frac{Z_2 - Z_1}{Z_2 + Z_1}\right)^2, \qquad T = \frac{Z_1}{Z_2} t_E^2 = \frac{4 Z_1 Z_2}{(Z_1 + Z_2)^2}, \qquad R + T = 1
Paper Q36: for Z2 = 2 Z1, r_E = 1/3 and t_E = 4/3 > 1! Yet R = 1/9 and T = (1/2)(16/9) = 8/9 -> R + T = 1! Larger E amplitude inside larger Z carries LESS current H!
Writing T = t_E^2 instead of (Z1/Z2) t_E^2 gives T = 16/9 > 1 — an instant violation of energy conservation whenever Z1 != Z2!

cards.title: Equal speed != zero reflection in magnetic matter (Q36c)
items: Can a boundary reflect waves even when BOTH media have the exact same wave speed v1 = v2 (same refractive index n1 = n2)? YES, if permeabilities differ!
Conversely, choosing mu2/mu1 = eps2/eps1 makes Z2 = Z1 so R = 0 (invisible Stealth/impedance-matched boundary) EVEN THOUGH wave speed drops across the boundary!
Nonmagnetic glass n = 1.5 in air (Z2 = Z0/1.5): r_E = -0.20 (pi phase flip on E!), R = 0.04 (4% reflection per face), T = 0.96.

cards.title: Quarter-wave anti-reflection transformer
items: To eliminate reflection completely between media Z1 and Z3 at target vacuum wavelength lambda_0, insert a lossless layer (index n_c, impedance Z_c) of thickness d:
Equal reflection amplitudes at front and back faces suffer round-trip phase shift 2 k_c d = pi, cancelling destructively in reflection so 100% power transmits!
If n1 < n_c < n3, BOTH front and back reflections carry the SAME pi phase flip, so destructive interference still requires 2 n_c d = lambda_0 / 2 (NOT lambda_0)!

title: Standing EM waves, mirror stress & cavity pressure u/3
subtitle: Constructing exact node structure in front of a conductor, magnetic Maxwell stress at a mirror, and 3D thermal photon gas.
takeaway: In a standing EM wave E and B oscillate 90 deg out of phase in BOTH space and time: <S> = 0, yet mirror magnetic pressure equals 2 I_inc / c.

cards.title: Standing wave in front of a perfect mirror (z <= 0)
items: Superpose E_i = E0 cos(kz - wt) x_hat (+z) and reflected E_r = -E0 cos(kz + wt) x_hat (-z) so tangential E vanishes on mirror z = 0 (Q31):
For E_r moving along -z with -E0 x_hat, (-z_hat) x (-x_hat) = +y_hat: reflected B ADDS at z = 0 instead of cancelling!
Node map: E nodes at z = -m lambda/2 (including mirror z = 0); B nodes at z = -(2m + 1) lambda/4 (quarter-wave shifted!).

cards.title: Zero mean Poynting vector vs nonzero mirror pressure
items: Multiply E and B: S_z = (2 E0^2 / Z0) sin(2kz) sin(2wt) sloshes energy back and forth every quarter-cycle with <S_z> = 0, while time-averaged density is spatially uniform:

\langle u\rangle = \varepsilon_0 E_0^2 = 2\langle u_{\mathrm{inc}}\rangle, \qquad P_{\mathrm{mirror}} = \left\langle\frac{B^2(0,t)}{2\mu_0}\right\rangle = \varepsilon_0 E_0^2 = \frac{2 I_{\mathrm{inc}}}{c}
At z = 0, E = 0 so surface currents feel Lorentz force (J_s x B_avg_across_sheet) equal to magnetic Maxwell stress B(0,t)^2 / (2 mu0), matching momentum reversal 2 I_inc / c!
Never write uE = uB in a standing wave: at wt = 0 ALL energy is magnetic; at wt = pi/2 ALL energy is electric!

cards.title: Isotropic cavity radiation: why pressure is u / 3
items: Fill an enclosure uniformly with isotropic radiation of total energy density u: solid angle dOmega carries density du = u dOmega/(4 pi) at angle theta to a specular wall:
Only half the rays move toward the wall (factor 1/2), and they strike at all angles with <cos^2(theta)> = 1/3: (1/2) * 2 * (1/3) u = u / 3 (vs u for a collimated beam)!
Careful boundary check (sec. 4.3): a cold black wall absorbing an isotropic field of total density u feels u / 6 until thermal equilibrium emission adds the second u / 6!

title: Conducting media, skin depth & collisionless plasmas
subtitle: Damped telegrapher wave equation, 45 deg B-to-E phase lag in metals, shielding attenuation, and ionospheric plasma cutoff.
takeaway: Good conductors (sigma >> w eps) damp fields exponentially in skin depth delta = sqrt(2/(mu sigma w)); collisionless plasmas reflect below w_p with v_p v_g = c^2 above.

cards.title: Wave equation in an Ohmic conductor (sec. 4.4)
items: Insert J_f = sigma E into Maxwell-Ampere inside a homogeneous conductor: curl B = mu sigma E + mu eps dE/dt. Taking curl of Faraday yields:
First time derivative breaks time-reversal symmetry (Ohmic dissipation!), making wavenumber k = k_R + i k_I complex so exp(i k z) = exp(i k_R z) exp(-k_I z) attenuates!
Poor-conductor limit (sigma << w eps, e.g. dry soil / seawater at high f): k_I ~ (sigma / 2) sqrt(mu/eps) = sigma Z / 2 is independent of frequency!

cards.title: Good-conductor skin depth delta & 45 deg magnetic lag
items: When conduction current dominates displacement current (sigma >> w eps), k^2 ~ i mu sigma w. Since sqrt(i) = (1 + i)/sqrt(2), k_R = k_I = 1/delta:
Three huge Olympiad consequences: (1) E decays by 1/e every delta and intensity I decays as exp(-2 z/delta); (2) B lags E by pi/4 (45 deg!); (3) magnetic energy uB >> uE inside metal!
Scale check in copper (sigma ~ 5.8e7 S/m): delta ~ 8.5 mm at 60 Hz, ~ 66 um at 1 MHz, and ~ 2.1 um at 1 GHz!

cards.title: Collisionless cold plasma dispersion & total reflection
items: In a neutralised gas of free electrons (number density n_e, mass m_e), Newton law m_e dv/dt = -e E gives J = -n_e e v = (i n_e e^2 / m_e w) E (purely inductive, ZERO heating!):
For w < w_p, eps_eff < 0 so k is purely imaginary: incident radio waves suffer 100% lossless reflection off the ionosphere or metals below UV plasma edge!

cards.title: Phase speed > c vs group speed < c check
items: Above plasma frequency (w > w_p), differentiate w^2 = w_p^2 + c^2 k^2 with respect to k to compare crest velocity v_p = w/k with packet/energy velocity v_g = dw/dk:
v_p = \frac{c}{\sqrt{1 - \omega_p^2/\omega^2}} > c, \qquad v_g = c\sqrt{1 - \frac{\omega_p^2}{\omega^2}} < c, \qquad v_p v_g = c^2
Relativity forbids signals/energy travelling faster than c — and group/signal velocity v_g stays strictly < c everywhere while crests slide faster along the envelope!
In dispersion problems, never plug phase index n = c/v_p < 1 into packet travel delay: radio pulsar dispersion delay uses t_arrival = L / v_g!

title: Relativistic Doppler, moving mirrors & waveguides
subtitle: Exact Lorentz light shift, double boost on moving mirrors, Poynting-Robertson orbital spiral, and parallel-plate TE modes.
takeaway: In vacuum no air frame exists: Doppler depends ONLY on relative beta = u/c, and a moving mirror shifts both frequency and radiation pressure by (1+beta)/(1-beta).
source: Source: Olympiad EM wave extensions (INPhO / IPhO standard)

cards.title: Relativistic optical Doppler & transverse time dilation
items: Because light requires no material medium, source-moving and observer-moving shifts are IDENTICAL and include Lorentz gamma = 1/sqrt(1 - beta^2), beta = u/c:
Even at closest approach (90 deg in observer frame), clock time dilation slows source oscillations by 1/gamma = sqrt(1 - beta^2) — a pure second-order redshift!
Low-speed check (beta << 1): df / f0 = +- beta + O(beta^2); astronomical redshift parameter 1 + z = lambda_obs / lambda_emit = sqrt((1+beta)/(1-beta)).

cards.title: Reflection & pressure on a moving flat mirror
items: A flat perfect mirror moves at speed u = beta c TOWARD an incoming normal vacuum beam of frequency f and intensity I (or minus sign if receding):
Two clean steps: mirror intercepts crests at relative speed c + u -> rate factor (1 + beta); reflected photon energy also jumps by (1 + beta)/(1 - beta), doing mechanical work on the beam!
Check beta -> -1 (mirror fleeing at light speed): f_ref -> 0 and P -> 0 because photons can never catch the mirror!

cards.title: Poynting-Robertson drag: why dust spirals INTO stars
items: A black dust grain of radius a in circular orbit at speed v around a star absorbs radial photons in the star frame, but re-emits thermally isotropically in its OWN rest frame:

In the star frame, forward-beamed thermal emission carries tangential momentum m_eff v = (P_abs/c^2) v away! Or equivalently in grain frame: stellar aberration tilts sunlight slightly head-on by angle v/c!
Result: angular momentum bleeds steadily so surviving micron grains (beta < 1/2) spiral inward over cosmic timescales.

cards.title: Parallel-plate metallic waveguide (TE_m modes)
items: Confine waves between two perfectly conducting plates at y = 0 and y = b: vanishing tangential E_z/E_x on both walls quantises k_y = m pi / b (integer m >= 1 for TE):
Picture a plane wave zig-zagging between walls at angle sin(theta_m) = w_c / w: crests slide faster along z (v_p = c / cos theta_m > c) while energy advances at v_g = c cos theta_m < c!
A hollow single-conductor pipe has NO TEM mode (m = 0): if lambda_0 > 2 b for parallel plates, ALL TE modes are cutoff and decay exponentially!
